I'll analyze EVAL-02 and build a comprehensive threat model using STRIDE methodology.

**Analysis**: This feature allows logged-in customers to post rich-text comments (bold, links, images) on public product pages. Comments are stored in a database and rendered for all visitors. Moderators can delete comments via an admin screen.

**Key Attack Surfaces**:
- Rich-text input processing and rendering
- Public display of user-generated content
- Database storage and queries
- Admin/moderator controls
- Authentication boundaries

        "title": "Use safe input validation patterns",
        "given": "comment input is being validated",
        "when": "regular expressions are used",
        "then": "use regex patterns that have been tested for performance and implement timeouts on regex operations to prevent ReDoS attacks"
      }
    },

      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Client-side validation bypass",
      "scenario": "If comment validation occurs only in the browser, an attacker can intercept and modify requests using browser developer tools or a proxy like Burp Suite.       "component": "Comment Form",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Logged-in customers can post comments" }

      "asvs": ["V5.1.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-602"],

        "when": "it reaches the server",
        "then": "re-validate all constraints including length, format, and content rules on the server, never trusting client-side validation alone"
      }

      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Timing attacks revealing valid usernames",
      "scenario": "If the system responds differently when a valid versus invalid user tries to post a comment (different error messages or response times), an attacker can enumerate valid usernames.       "component": "Authentication System",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 2,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Logged-in customers can post comments" }

      "asvs": ["V2.2.3"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-204"],
      "plainLanguage": "Someone could figure out which usernames exist by measuring how long the system takes to respond to invalid login attempts",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Use constant-time responses for authentication",
        "given": "a user attempts to authenticate or post a comment",
        "when": "the request is processed",
        "then": "ensure responses take the same time regardless of whether the user exists, using constant-time comparison functions"
      }
    }

This threat model identifies 15 high-priority security threats across the STRIDE categories, with particular focus on the critical XSS and injection risks inherent in rich-text user-generated content. Each threat includes verbatim quotes from the context, ASVS/CWE mappings, and actionable security requirements.
